svg.title: Shoot 4 (tips the HIVE, 1 spare), take 3 GARDEN POLLEN, step off the wall - RED alliance
svg.desc: Top view of the 141.35 by 141.35 inch BIOBUZZ field, audience at the bottom, red alliance on the left. Route garden_cycle for the RED alliance, starting in tile B1, with 6 steps: 1 START at (35.0, 9.8, -90 deg); 2 SHOOT 4 at UP cell from the solver's pose; 3 DRIVE to GARDEN constant to 9.0, 18.0; 4 DRIVE into GARDEN constant to 9.0, 10.6; 5 INTAKE GARDEN +3 from (9.0, 10.6, -90 deg); 6 DRIVE off the wall constant to 20.0, 24.0. First tip: we shoot the first tip. Estimated 13.8 s, POLLEN balance -1, up to 23 points for our robot; 0 errors and 1 warnings.
svg.text: Shoot 4 (tips the HIVE, 1 spare), take 3 GARDEN POLLEN, step off the wall - RED alliance
id garden_cycle | start tile B1 | 6 steps | red ink | first tip: we shoot the first tip

g.title: Where a robot facing -90 degrees may be set up (rule G304): the tinted stretches of the own walls. The gaps are the FLOWERS, the LOADING ZONE, the corners and the center line.
g.text: tinted: where this start may stand (G304)

g.title: step 2: move to the pose of SHOOT

step 3: DRIVE to GARDEN constant to 9.0, 18.0 (t = 6.8 to 8.7 s) - Slides along the audience wall with the intake still facing it. The robot's side edge is only 0.1 in from the red wall all the way to the GARDEN and back (by design, so that the wheel can reach the POLLEN): touching a wall is legal, but a heading error of about half a degree would press a corner into it.
step 4: DRIVE into GARDEN constant to 9.0, 10.6 (t = 8.7 to 9.6 s) - Front edge ends 0.8 in from the wall, on the row of POLLEN (x 0..12).
step 6: DRIVE off the wall constant to 20.0, 24.0 (t = 12.6 to 13.8 s) - Ends with the whole footprint more than 1.5 in off every wall: LEAVE.

step 1: START at (35.0, 9.8, -90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - Front edge ON the audience wall (the center of rotation is 9.77 in out). Place the robot with the wheel tips touching the wall and the middle of the robot over tile B1.

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from the solver's pose (t = 0.0 to 6.8 s) - AUTO pose: the solver moves from B1 to the standoff pose in front of the UP cell. The 3 staged NECTAR plus the 3rd POLLEN tip the HIVE and the 4th pre-load is probably spent (the feeder stops only about 0.85 s after the tip); the REAR cell is the UP one from now on. - pose drawn is the nominal standoff pose; the solver picks the real one

step 5: INTAKE GARDEN +3 from (9.0, 10.6, -90 deg) (t = 9.6 to 12.6 s) - NOT MEASURED YET (day one): at this pose a flat wheel disc sits over two GARDEN POLLEN (its middle is 1.6 to 1.7 in from them, and a wheel and a POLLEN need 2.8 in between their middles), so which 3 of the 4 are taken, the +3 and the 2.5 s are placeholders until the intake is tried on the real GARDEN. The 4 GARDEN POLLEN lie along the wall at x 1.40, 4.29, 7.18 and 10.07 (CAD). The robot holds 0 (the spare pre-load was probably spent) or 1 (the feeder stopped in time) and takes 3, so it carries 3 or 4 into TELEOP; 4 is the most it may hold (G407), so the intake never takes a 4th.
step 6: DRIVE off the wall constant to 20.0, 24.0 (t = 12.6 to 13.8 s) - Ends with the whole footprint more than 1.5 in off every wall: LEAVE.

POLLEN: hold 4 at start, +3 taken, -4 fired, 3 at the end (balance -1) | Validator: 0 ERROR, 1 WARN

g.title: WARN step 2 [G417] step 2 (SHOOT, the move to its pose): the HIVE tips with POLLEN 3 of the 4 (3 NECTAR in the cell; a cell tips at 8 POLLEN-equivalents (each POLLEN counts 1, each NECTAR 5/3)), but the camera cannot stop the feeder at once: the POLLEN that tips it is in the air for 0.50 s and the feeder stops about 0.85 s after it lands (Auto.TIP_STOP_LATENCY_SEC), while the next POLLEN leaves 1.00 s after the last. So the next 1 POLLEN will probably be launched into the cell while it swings down (G417: a launch at a rocking HIVE can spoil the tip; QA12 lets you add elements to a HIVE that is moving) and is spent: the plan counts 4 fired and 0 of the spare kept. The spare is for a field that needs one more POLLEN, not a POLLEN to carry on. Fire only 3 to keep it for sure (no spare then), or measure the real stop time on day one: with a latency under 0.50 s the spare stays in the robot
